state.policy_text: Covered: failure of a covered part caused by a defect in materials or workmanship under normal use. Not covered as wear: gradual deterioration of a part from normal use over time, including wear items such as brake pads, wiper blades, belts, and clutch linings. Not covered as external damage: damage from collision, road hazards, flood, fire, animals, misuse, or repairs performed by others.

state.policy_text: Defect: a flaw in materials or workmanship present when the part left the factory, causing failure under normal operation with no outside cause. Wear: gradual deterioration from normal use over time and mileage, including bearings, bushings, belts, and friction surfaces reaching the end of their service life. External damage: failure caused by an outside event or action, including collision, road debris, flood, fire, animal contact, misuse, or improper repair or installation performed by anyone other than this shop.
state.narrative: Alternator bearing seized at 41,000 miles. Bearing race shows some normal polishing consistent with mileage. Found the serpentine belt tensioner had been replaced by another shop and installed with the belt routed over the wrong pulley, putting a heavy side load on the alternator pulley. In my judgment the incorrect prior belt installation caused the bearing to seize; the polishing did not contribute.

rationale: The narrative mentions both normal wear and an improper prior installation by another shop, which the policy defines as external damage, and it states which one caused the failure; the contract says to select the stated cause when more than one is described and the narrative names the cause.
